rationale: The candidate reads as a single compact mass with a recognizable carved central void and a clear upper/ground hierarchy, so it is more coherent than fragmented. The open space is legible in plan and the mass does respond to the parcel rather than merely filling a box. The road frontage edge is acknowledged by the void/cut, though the response is still somewhat generic and not maximally public. The silhouette is not a stair-step cliché, but the roof/section remains relatively flat and blocky compared with the best neighborhood-living precedents, so section-program fit is only moderate. Overall the form is program-appropriate for compact neighborhood living and resonates well with the similar references, while needing stronger section articulation and a cleaner, more intentional access-side threshold.
